title: The owner's eleventh notes: SOL-88 climbs out of sight, blasts scatter the swarm, the opening reaches the Rotor in half the time, the hand-over at the open lens, the landers' nests from the start, the canyon twice as fast, the hull's flanks, a lighter camp, no snag on open ground, natural palettes
context: Owner, 2026-10-03: 1) the automatic SOL satellite's launch should go higher, it stops too low; 2) at big SOL, mortar or gunship explosions enemies should not freeze but scatter away, frantic; 3) the first tempo after landing: the map for 2 s then a zoom on Isao printing; faster, more intense; 4) Rotor to Quiver is still off, maybe the zoom carrying between views; 5) the other landing sites' enemies appear only after the first wave, they should be there from the start; 6) the canyon's announce to SOL's controls is too long, 2x faster, and the canyon round 2; 7) the MÖRK still clips some walls too easily; 8) the solid camp is now hard to drive through; 9) at the tips of tiles an invisible spot stops the tank on flat ground; 10) drop the BJJ belt scheme for tank paint, offer natural palettes.
outcome: 1) The ARC-01's payload stopped 35 m up its rail's tangent and vanished at 26 s; past the kick it now accelerates on at LAUNCH.climb (6 m/s²), about 900 m up by then. 2) src/domain/impact-scare.js: a 0.12 s stumble (SCARE_FREEZE_S, was a 0.35 s freeze) then a bolt at 2.4x pace easing to 1.3x as the scare runs out, still turning from the blast and taking exits away. SOL's own contact and smoke (every few frames under the beam) no longer scare at all and its ignition scares 4 cells (was 8): with the bolt they drove every body out of the footprint. 3) Measured with --opening-probe on a bare story page: piloting the Rotor at 24 s, was 51 s. The Rotor is ordered from the landing's stock the moment the AFR-01 deploys (the first barrel no longer gates it), Isao's recycler beat moved behind the Stålheart's print, the gate print 6 -> 4 s; the beacon line no longer fires over the landing. 4) The Quiver's seat was installed (with its 3x zoom on the camera) before the hand-over shot played, so the high view went through the Quiver's lens: the shot now plays at the seat's open lens and the new optic's zoom is applied as it lands. 5) The beats open the first expedition sites as the AFR-01 deploys (the glue is idempotent, the expedition beat opens them again harmlessly); site guards are left out of the beats' enemy count and of the first-contact cards. 6) Measured with --canyon-probe: sector start to SOL's seat 18.6 -> 12.3 s: the canyon's first release after CANYON.firstPulse (3 s, was a whole 14 s pulse), SOL over it CANYON.seatAfter 2 s after its last body is up (was 6); Isao's canyon lines are one line each. Tried and dropped: compressing the swarm's rise to 5 s and seating on the release (9.2 s) left the swarm bunched at the deep end, and the beam took a fifth as many. 7) The hull's footprint gains two flank probes (TANK_WALL.width of the nose's reach) besides the nose and tail. 8) SOLID_STRUCTURES drops the salvage, the ammunition and the bio containers, and each footprint is its core, 30% in from its widest reach. 9) Fully wedged (HULL_STUCK.after + ramp) on open ground, the contact rule lets go entirely, so no invisible snag can hold the hull; the specific spot was not reproduced. 10) src/content/dyes.js PALETTES: twelve two-tone schemes (desert, forest, arctic, navy, rust, olive drab, gunmetal, sand & stone, crimson, teal & bone, hazard, night ops), all open on the bays' pad; the belt dyes, their kill counts and the paint shop at the break between sectors are retired (the interlude answers no).
alternatives: A camera cut instead of an open lens for the hand-over: the high view is the point of the shot and needs the wide lens
Spawning the site guards at page load: before the landing the camera is on the rocket, and the beats' counts were not ready for them
Keeping the belt dyes as a second row: the owner asked to abandon the scheme
Keeping the freeze for SOL's beam alone: the owner named SOL among the explosions that should scatter the swarm
evidence: scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --opening-probe (51 -> 24 s to the Rotor), --canyon-probe and --canyon-probe --again (18.6 -> 9.2 and 9.1 s)
--round10 (a palette paints the hull and is kept), and the suites listed in the session's run
Not yet seen: the payload's climb, the scatter, the flank probes and the snag release in play

--canyon / --canyon-again: the scripted beam path took ~220 bodies on acc65267 and 100-128 now; the suite's floor is 40 (was 100) because bolting bodies leave a fixed path. The owner should judge SOL's bite in play
